targetName: Soi LED Floodlight on Utility Pole

terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: concrete distribution pole with a short insulator crossarm and a clamped flat LED flood panel
motionPotential: none - a direct-buried concrete pole, rigid body
objectClass.notes: The informal soi lighting variant: a cheap flat LED flood clamped to an ordinary distribution pole. The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.310 against the declared 0.053, so it carries the fixture and not the assembly proportions, and the declared 0.45 x 8.5 x 0.55 m envelope is narrow enough that only a SHORT crossarm stub fits - the plate's full-width distribution crossarm is outside this asset's declared envelope.

reasoning: Four drawn parts: the concrete pole, a short insulator crossarm, the clamped flood housing and its lens.

The crossarm's four insulators are SWELLINGS on the crossarm's own swept spine, not four components and not a repetition system: a radial repetition places instances around a circle, and these sit in a LINE along the arm.
No baseplate and no bolts: a distribution pole is direct-buried.
No moving parts, so one root pivot and no sockets.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate. Four drawn parts and the sub-structure - taper, bracket clamp, arm rise, lantern wedge, bowl seating - carried as localFeatures because each component costs a draw call.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: A tapered square section 0.225 m at the foot and 0.140 m at the top.
A chamfered cap closing the pole's top on all four faces.
Fourteen recessed lifting and fixing holes down one face.
Green algae over the bottom 3.2 m as an axis tint on the concrete.
Four cream porcelain pin insulators on a single crossarm.
A plain rectangular slab tilted 35 degrees nose-down, with a bezel proud of its face.
A band and a 75 mm stub instead of an arm, so the panel hangs tight against the pole.
An 18-band diode array recessed behind the bezel.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The pole section is square: the plate shows flat faces meeting at vertical arrises. Confidence 0.85.
The far side of the pole and housing is mirrored; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.

The plate's distribution crossarm is much wider than the declared 0.55 m depth envelope. The envelope governs, so the crossarm is built as a 0.55 m stub carrying four insulators rather than the full-width arm in the plate. Confidence 0.8.
Conductors, cabling and the clamp band are not built: thin geometry the budget cannot carry. Confidence 0.9.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: the flood reads as a flat slab, not a wedge
per-material rendered luma against the measured 146/120/140
turntable hole gate at all four azimuths
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not take proportion from the plate or the proxy.
Do not build the plate's full-width distribution crossarm; it is outside the declared 0.55 m depth envelope.
Do not give this pole a baseplate or bolts - it is direct-buried.
Do not build the flood as a cobra head; the two soi variants exist to be different.
Do not make the lens emissive, and do not seat it flush with the housing face.
qualityContract.depthRationale: FOUR components across four material layers: the pole, its crossarm and the flood housing as macro, the lens as meso. Eight micro-feature groups sit inside them -- square taper, chamfered cap, cast holes, algae band, the insulator row, the no-outreach band-and-stub, the tilted slab and the recessed lens.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 0.45 x 8.50 x 0.55 m within the asset's 10% tolerance.

featureReviewTargets.name: Square tapered concrete pole
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Four flat faces with vertical arrises, narrowing monotonically.

featureReviewTargets.name: Flat LED flood, not a cobra head
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The head must be a PLAIN RECTANGULAR SLAB with a bezel and a recessed lens, hanging tight against the pole on a band and a stub with NO outreach arm. A shaped lantern, or any arm, is the wrong prop -- those are the two give-aways the asset notes lead with.

featureReviewTargets.name: Insulator crossarm
featureReviewTargets.criteria: ONE crossarm carrying a short row of porcelain pin insulators. Two arms would be the formal soi variant, not this one.

featureReviewTargets.name: Material response and the hole gate
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Concrete, steel, housing and lens must separate by value against the measured 146 / 120 / 140, and NO surface may render near the ~58 backdrop.

featureReviewTargets.name: Algae staining
featureReviewTargets.criteria: A green-grey band over the lower pole fading out by about 3.4 m.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: concrete 146 / crossarm steel 120 / housing 140 / lens brightest, in measured plate luma.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as four named parts. Not articulated and not breakable.

assumptions: The pole section is square: flat faces meeting at vertical arrises in the plate. Confidence 0.85.
The far side of the pole and housing is mirrored; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.
The crossarm is built as a 0.55 m stub because the declared depth envelope is 0.55 m; the plate's full-width distribution arm is outside this asset's envelope.
The housing's heatsink fins are NOT built: sub-pixel at 7.3 m and each would need geometry the budget cannot carry.
No conductors, cabling or clamp bands are modelled.
The lens is opaque and NOT emissive: the factory ships no lights, and an emissive lens would double-count against the level's lighting.
Metalness is authored below a physical 1.0 on the metals because the harness carries no environment map.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: base-center: the origin sits at the centre of the pole's square section on the ground plane. Direct-buried, so there is no baseplate.

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 0.449 x 8.500 x 0.550 m against the declared 0.45 x 8.5 x 0.55 -- exact on all three. Depth is the crossarm span; width is the pole plus the slab's far corner and nothing else, because this variant has no outreach arm.
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral about the XY plane (z=0) for the housing, and about the YZ plane for the crossarm
silhouette.notes: The declared envelope is narrow enough that the plate's full-width distribution crossarm does not fit; it is built as a 0.55 m stub carrying the insulator row.

componentTree.name: Tapered square prestressed pole with cast holes and algae
componentTree.topologyRationale: A tapered SQUARE frustum, not a cylinder -- 12 triangles for the whole shaft, which leaves the crossarm, its insulators and the flood slab affordable as real geometry.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin base-center, +Y up. One frustum 0.225 m square at the foot tapering to 0.140 m, chamfered cap, fourteen recessed cast holes down the +Z face between 1.15 and 7.00 m, algae as an axis tint over the bottom 3.2 m.

localFeatures.description: 0.225 m square at the base tapering to 0.140 m. Proportion from the DECLARATION: silh.mjs puts the plate's subject at 285 x 919 px, implying 2.48 m of width at 8.5 m tall against the declared 0.45.
A short frustum pulling in on all four faces at the top.
Fourteen recessed lifting and fixing holes down one face, as recesses rather than through-holes.
Green algae over the bottom 3.2 m as an axis tint multiplied into the concrete.

componentTree.notes: Shared verbatim with the other two concrete poles in this kit.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Cast concrete carrying its cap, hole recesses and algae as vertex colours, with spalled patches as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Crossarm with four pin insulators
componentTree.topologyRationale: ONE arm, not the two the formal soi lamp carries -- that is part of what separates the two variants, and the previous build had neither.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.055 x 0.045 m steel channel spanning 0.55 m along Z -- the declared depth IS the crossarm span -- carrying four pin insulators.

localFeatures.description: Four cream porcelain pin insulators, each a skirt disc under a head disc. FOUR rather than the formal variant's six per arm, and one arm rather than two, which is what the declared 0.55 m depth encodes.

componentTree.notes: Steel #9a8f80 and porcelain #d8d2bc as vertex colours on one material.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Weathered channel steel carrying its porcelain insulators as a vertex colour.

componentTree.name: Flat LED slab on a banded L bracket
componentTree.topologyRationale: A plain rectangular SLAB with a bezel, not a shaped lantern, hanging TIGHT against the pole -- the two give-aways the asset notes name. It is a third material because a painted aluminium panel is neither concrete nor weathered channel steel.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A band round the pole at 7.25 m, a 75 mm stub bracket, and a 0.30 x 0.29 m slab tilted 0.62 rad nose-down with a bezel frame proud of its face. Panel centre at x 0.196 so the far corner lands on the declared 0.45 m width.

localFeatures.description: NO outreach arm: a band and a 75 mm stub, so the slab hangs against the pole. This is the whole reason the declared width is 0.45 m against the formal variant's 1.6, and it is the give-away the asset notes lead with.
A plain rectangular slab tilted 35 degrees nose-down toward the alley, with a bezel frame standing proud of its face. A shaped lantern would be the wrong prop.

componentTree.notes: Housing #8f979b at luma 146 and its bezel #7c8488, both clear of the erased luma window.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Painted aluminium slab and bezel, cooler than the crossarm steel and quite unlike the concrete.

componentTree.name: LED lens face
componentTree.topologyRationale: The lens is separate ONLY so its diode-band tile has somewhere to live: a tile binds per MATERIAL, and on the housing material the band pattern would print across the casting and the bracket too.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.272 x 0.262 m pane 8 mm thick set inside the bezel, sharing the slab's tilt.

localFeatures.description: Set INSIDE the bezel rather than flush with its face: co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight, and a real panel's lens sits behind its frame. It carries an 18-band tile as the diode array.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A pale diode array behind a diffuser, carried as an 18-band canvas tile bound after construction.

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: Shared with the other concrete poles in this kit; their plate subject masks read p50 118,114,102 and 127,126,121, luma 114-126.

localOverrides.description: Green-grey staining as a vertex-colour axis-band (y -0.05..2.40, softness 1.00) authored at #8A8870, lifted from the measured #6e6d5f for the hole-gate margin.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.449 x 8.500 x 0.550 m against the declared 0.45 x 8.5 x 0.55 -- exact on all three axes. Depth is the crossarm span; width is the pole plus the slab's far corner and nothing else, because this variant has no outreach arm. Proportion comes from the DECLARATION: silh.mjs puts the plate's subject at 285 x 919 px, implying 2.48 m of width at 8.5 m tall.

A tapered SQUARE frustum 0.225 m at the foot to 0.140 m at the top, chamfered cap, fourteen recessed cast holes down one face. The previous build was a bare smooth pipe with none of it. The shaft is 12 triangles as one frustum, which is why the crossarm, its insulators and the slab are all real geometry at 4% of the triangle ceiling.

A plain rectangular slab tilted 35 degrees nose-down with a bezel proud of its face and a recessed 18-band lens, carried on a steel band and a 75 mm stub with NO outreach arm. Both give-aways the asset notes lead with are now legible; the previous build had a tiny featureless box and no bracket, bezel or lens at all. The plate's panel stands slightly further off the pole than mine, which the declared 0.45 m width does not allow.

ONE crossarm spanning the declared 0.55 m depth with four cream porcelain pin insulators, each a skirt disc under a head disc. One arm and four insulators rather than the formal soi variant's two arms of six -- that difference is what the declared depth encodes, and the previous build had no arm and no insulators.

Four material layers: weathered concrete #9a998f, crossarm steel carrying its porcelain as a vertex colour, painted panel aluminium #8f979b and the lens. The housing is authored at luma 146 deliberately -- gatecrop's erased band is 55.5-60.5, a narrow window rather than a floor, and a face renders between about 0.55 and 1.0 of its albedo, so the safe range is luma < 55 or > 110. NOT carried: the plate's rust bleed from the crossarm bolts, which is directional where the tile is isotropic.

Green algae over the bottom 3.2 m as an axis tint multiplied into the concrete rather than a second material, with spalled patches as a post-construction tile on the same material. The plate's spalling is heavier and more clustered low down than the isotropic tile gives.

Green algae over the bottom 3.2 m as an axis tint multiplied into the concrete rather than a second material, with spalled patches as a post-construction tile on the same material. The plate's spalling is heavier and more clustered low down than the isotropic tile gives.

Measured bbox 0.449 x 8.500 x 0.550 m against the declared 0.45 x 8.5 x 0.55 -- exact on all three axes. Proportion comes from the DECLARATION: silh.mjs puts the plate's subject at 285 x 919 px, implying 2.48 m of width at 8.5 m tall.

A tapered SQUARE frustum 0.225 m at the foot to 0.140 m at the top, chamfered cap, fourteen recessed cast holes down one face. The previous build was a bare smooth pipe with none of it. One arm and four insulators rather than the formal soi variant's two arms of six -- that difference is what the declared depth encodes, and the previous build had no arm and no insulators.

Four material layers: weathered concrete #9a998f, crossarm steel carrying its porcelain as a vertex colour, painted panel aluminium #8f979b and the lens. The housing is authored at luma 146 deliberately -- gatecrop's erased band is 55.5-60.5, a narrow window rather than a floor, and a face renders between about 0.55 and 1.0 of its albedo, so the safe range is luma < 55 or > 110. NOT carried: the plate's rust bleed from the crossarm bolts, which is directional where the tile is isotropic.

Green algae over the bottom 3.2 m as an axis tint multiplied into the concrete rather than a second material, with spalled patches as a post-construction tile on the same material. The plate's spalling is heavier and more clustered low down than the isotropic tile gives.

reviewHistory.summary: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 0.449 x 8.5 x 0.55 m. Cost: 656 triangles / 16000, 4 draw calls / 12, 4 materials / 8, 4 unique geometries / 16, 2 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 1.0, 0.986, 1.018], interior hole fractions [0.0003, 0.0, 0.0001, 0.0]).  Four components at 4 draw calls, 4 materials and 4 geometries against a hero2x ceiling of 12/8/16 -- 4% of the triangle ceiling, because the pole is 12 triangles as one frustum.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Raised to hero2x with the lighting kit and deliberately underspent: 656 triangles at 4 draw calls, 4 materials and 4 geometries -- 4% of the triangle ceiling. The pole is 12 triangles as one frustum.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left; the pole's left face reads brighter than its right.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides lifted rather than black, roughly a 0.7 shadow-to-key ratio.
No separate rim in the plate - the object separates from the backdrop by value alone.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A near-white seamless backdrop at luma ~241; foreground coverage is 7.5%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
